cases.report:
# Queue behavior

Kestrel v2 retries are disabled by default. [1.1]

Kestrel v2 cannot cancel running jobs. [1.1]

sources.text: Kestrel is a fictional queue scheduler. In Kestrel v1, each queue permits exactly one dispatcher and leases expire after 30 seconds. In Kestrel v2, leases expire after 60 seconds. Kestrel v2 permits two dispatchers only if each owns a different queue partition; two dispatchers on the same partition are forbidden. Retries in Kestrel v2 are disabled by default and can be enabled explicitly. Kestrel v2 can cancel queued jobs but cannot cancel a running job. Kestrel v2 accepts jobs in JSON, with an optional priority field; an example is {"priority":2}. This handbook supplies no throughput measurements or power-loss guarantees.
sources.version: Kestrel v1 and v2, explicitly distinguished

cases.report:
# Export prerequisite

Morrow v2 exports recordings only while online. [1.1]

sources.text: Morrow is a fictional sensor recorder. Morrow v1 retains the latest 24 samples in volatile memory and timestamps them in UTC. Morrow v2 retains the latest 48 samples and timestamps them in UTC. In Morrow v2, durable storage requires explicitly enabling the durable flag; the flag is off by default. Both Morrow v1 and Morrow v2 export recordings only while online; offline export is unavailable. Morrow v2 exports CSV. This manual provides no battery-life specification or sensor-accuracy measurement.
